'''Business and economy'''
*[[Economic impact of the 2026 Iran war]]
**[[International sanctions against Iran]]
***[[United States Secretary of the Treasury|U.S. treasury secretary]] [[Scott Bessent]] announces that the U.S. will temporarily lift sanctions on [[Petroleum industry in Iran|Iranian oil]] at sea in an effort to ease energy supply pressures. The temporary relief will last for 30 days until April 19. [https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/mar/20/us-sanctions-iranian-oil (''The Guardian'')]
**The [[United States Energy Department|U.S. energy department]] says it has awarded contracts to loan a first batch of 45.2 million barrels of crude oil from the [[Strategic Petroleum Reserve (United States)|Strategic Petroleum Reserve]]. [https://www.businesstimes.com.sg/international/us-loans-45-2-million-barrels-strategic-reserve-oil-first-batch-iran-war (''The Business Times'')] 
**[[Philippine Airlines]] announces it will halt flights to the [[Middle East]] until April 30 due to safety concerns regarding the Iran war. [https://manilastandard.net/news/314718005/pal-halts-middle-east-flights-until-april-30.html (''Manila Standard'')]

**A [[Juries in the United States|United States jury]] in a civil trial finds that [[X (social network)|X (formerly Twitter)]] chairperson [[Elon Musk]] misled investors in two [[Tweet (social media)|tweets]], but absolves him of some [[fraud]] allegations. [https://www.dw.com/en/elon-musk-misled-twitter-shareholders-us-jury-finds/a-76462448 (DW)] [https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2026-03-20/jury-finds-elon-musk-misled-investors-during-twitter-purchase-absolves-him-of-some-fraud-claims (''Los Angeles Times'')]
